answer: Continuous reputation decay with shared pool liability: each identity's score is a decaying vine, requiring recurring useful work to stay above a visibility threshold, and all identities traced to one operator share a single liability pool. Cloning forces the attacker to sustain work and absorb every clone's penalties together. Honest operators pay only normal upkeep, cheaper than mass clone maintenance. A fable of cheap duplication collapses; saffron fees accrue per sustained identity.
